title: Convolutional CRFs for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Fully connected CRF made local (conditional independence outside a window) so mean-field inference is a convolution; over 100x faster and all kernel parameters learnable by backprop.
evidence: R: >100x speed-up over FullCRF for inference and training (abstract). R (from rNCA table): DenseCRF on DRIVE vessels: Dice 0.761 -> 0.760, dBeta0 0.965 -> 0.712 (fewer fragments).
adaptation: Inactive arm: bilateral intensity + position kernel on the ensemble softmax so partial inactive detections expand to the uniform dark region bounded by cracks (inactive is dark, blobby, well labelled, recall 0.61). Crack arm: small spatial kernel only, as a test of whether snapping to the dark ridge helps or hurts strict IoU (labels sit off the ridge). Kernel weights fit on val / OOF; base model unchanged.
min_experiment: Arm: ConvCRF/DenseCRF on house ensemble softmax (and PF ensemble on E1). Baseline: house ensemble argmax. Metrics: inactive IoU and recall on clean-49 and OOF CV, E1 inactive IoU, crack relF1@2 as a guard. Kill: inactive IoU < +0.02 on OOF CV or crack relF1@2 drop > 0.005.
prior_overlap: none. Inference-side runs were ensemble, logit bias, BN adaptation, intensity normalisation, per-module thresholds; no CRF.
